newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-CAMPBELL ENSURES FINE START FOR ZIMBABWE IN FIRST TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAMPBELL ENSURES FINE START FOR ZIMBABWE IN FIRST TEST.

text.p: Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell ensured his side did not squander first use of a bland Queen's Club wicket on the opening day of the inaugural test match against England on Wednesday.
At lunch Campbell, who had won the toss and elected to bat on a steamy morning, had scored 70 out of Zimbabwe's 109 for one after opener Stuart Carlisle was dismissed for a third ball duck.

Left-hander Campbell took the attack to the bowlers after his team had lost their first wicket to the 10th ball of the innings. At the interval he had had scored his ninth half-century in test cricket with 11 fours from 102 balls.

Opener Grant Flower, playing the anchor role, compiled a sedate 34 not out in a second wicket partnership of 106 after Carlisle had pushed a ball from Darren Gough straight into the hands of John Crawley at short leg.
England omitted paceman Andy Caddick from their line up, giving a test debut to Yorkshire seamer Chris Silverwood.
Zimbabwe were forced to make a late change when Eddo Brandes twisted his ankle at practice. He was replaced by left arm seamer Bryan Strang.
